question: What is the correct symbol for the element sodium?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Na**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical symbol for **Sodium** is **Na**. This symbol is derived from its **Latin** name, **Natrium**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• Sodium is a chemical element with the **atomic number 11**, which means it contains **11 protons** in its atomic nucleus.
 
• It is located in **Group 1** of the **Periodic Table**, placing it among the **Alkali Metals**.
 
• In terms of its position, it is found in **Period 3** and the **s-block** of the modern periodic table.
 
• The **atomic mass** of Sodium is approximately **22.989 u**.
 
• Under standard conditions of **temperature and pressure**, sodium is a **soft**, **silvery-white**, and **highly reactive** metal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Physical Properties:**
 
 
• Sodium is so **soft** that it can be easily cut with a **knife** at **room temperature**.
 
• It has a **density** of **0.97 g/cm³**, which makes it **less dense than water**, allowing it to float.
 
• Its **melting point** is relatively low for a metal, at **97.79°C** (**208.02°F**), and its **boiling point** is **883°C**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Reactivity:**
 
 
• Sodium is extremely **reactive**, particularly with **water**. When it comes into contact with water, it reacts **exothermically** to produce **sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** and flammable **hydrogen gas**.
 
• Due to this high reactivity, sodium is never found as a **pure element** in nature; it must be stored under **mineral oil** or **kerosene** to prevent reaction with **moisture** or **oxygen** in the air.
 
 
 
• **Industrial and Domestic Uses:**
 
 
• The most common compound is **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, which is used globally as **table salt** and for **de-icing roads**.
 
• **Sodium Carbonate (Na2CO3)**, also known as **washing soda**, is vital in the manufacture of **glass**, **paper**, and **detergents**.
 
• **Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO3)**, or **baking soda**, is widely used in the **food industry** and as a **fire extinguisher** component.
 
 
 
• **Biological Importance:**
 
 
• Sodium is an **essential electrolyte** for the human body. It is critical for maintaining **osmotic pressure**, **fluid balance**, and the **transmission of nerve impulses**.
 
• The **sodium-potassium pump** is a vital mechanism in **cell biology** that moves ions across **cell membranes**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Origin of the Name:** The element was first isolated by **Humphry Davy** in the year **1807** through the **electrolysis** of **caustic soda (NaOH)**.
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **S** is the chemical symbol for **Sulfur** (atomic number **16**), which is a **non-metal**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Sd** and **So** are not valid chemical symbols for any known element in the **IUPAC** periodic table. ***Hence, options 2 and 4 are incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Valency:** Sodium has a **valency of 1** because it has **one electron** in its **outermost shell** (electron configuration: **2, 8, 1**). It tends to lose this electron to achieve a **stable octet configuration**, forming a **cation (Na+)**.
 
• **Abundance:** Sodium is the **sixth most abundant element** in the **Earth's crust**, making up about **2.6%** of its mass.
